memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a
layer of dew around the camp. When the dew was gone, thin flakes like frost on
the ground appeared on the desert floor. When the Israelites saw it, they said
to each other, 'What is it?' For they did not know what it was."
- Ex 16:13-15a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"What is it?" That question became the name of the food. The word "manna" comes
from that very phrase.

For forty years, Israel ate something whose name was a question.

There is something wonderful in that. God's provision arrived in a form they
could not identify or explain. It did not fit any category they had. They could
not have asked for it, because they did not know it existed.

We often pray with limited imagination. We ask God for the solutions we can
already picture, the specific job, the particular outcome, the door we have
identified. And God sometimes answers with something we would never have named.

Paul writes that God "is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or
imagine" (Eph 3:20). Notice both words. More than we ask, and more than we can
imagine.

Israel wanted the pots of meat they remembered. God gave them bread from heaven
they had never heard of.

If God's answer to your prayer has arrived in an unrecognisable form, look at it
more carefully before you reject it. It may be exactly the provision, arriving
under a name you did not expect.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has God answered a prayer in a form you did not recognise at first?
2. Are your prayers limited to solutions you can already picture?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for asking only for what I can imagine. Help me to recognise
Your provision even when it arrives in an unfamiliar form. Amen.
